questions.q: For this exact tied-head GPT, which expression counts all unique learned parameters?
questions.why: The embedding/head matrix is counted once. Each block includes attention and MLP matrices, their biases and two affine LayerNorms. The final norm adds 2C. S is position capacity, not actual sequence length T.

questions.q: At fixed embedding width, what does doubling the number of full attention heads do to this model's parameter count?
choices: Leaves it unchanged, if the head count divides the width
questions.why: Heads partition the same total Q/K/V width. The projection matrix shapes do not change. Attention score storage and head dimensions can change.

questions.q: What has the GPT-2-shaped meta-device check demonstrated?
choices: The local module has the expected tensor shapes and unique parameter count without allocating weight data
GPT-2 trains in under a second
questions.why: Meta tensors hold metadata, not learned numeric values. Counting is not training, inference or checkpoint parity.

questions.q: Which interpretation of 16P bytes is correct in the lab?
choices: Exact peak memory for any AdamW training run
All deployment memory including KV cache
Logical bytes for FP32 weights, gradients and two FP32 Adam moment arrays, excluding other memory
questions.why: Each of those four arrays uses four bytes per parameter. Activations, masks, temporaries, scalar optimizer state, runtime and allocator overhead are excluded.

questions.q: What is the safest conclusion from the constructed loss table?
choices: Every production model needs exactly four data units
A fixed compute product can favor a balanced allocation under the stated chosen objective
questions.why: The exponents, coefficients and floor are chosen for teaching. Real scaling relations require controlled training runs, validation measurements, fitting and held-out confirmation.

questions.q: In Part 1, untie the toy output head by cloning its weights. What are the unique parameter count and the added count?
questions.why: The new independent matrix has V*C = 9*8 = 72 entries. Copying initial values does not preserve Parameter identity.

questions.q: For Part 4, increase actual context from 512 to 1,024 at batch 1 with the same GPT-2-shaped model. What changes?
questions.answer: The one-layer dense score matrix grows from 3,145,728 to 12,582,912 elements, a factor of four. The hypothetical all-layer two-byte KV cache grows from 18,874,368 to 37,748,736 bytes, a factor of two. Parameter count stays fixed.
questions.why: Scores contain T*T pairs; the full multi-head KV cache stores one key and one value vector per position per layer. Position capacity is already 1,024.

questions.q: Hold the rough 6ND budget at 600,000,000,000,000 FLOPs. After increasing N from 1,000,000 to 2,000,000, how many processed tokens D fit?
questions.why: The product ND stays fixed. Doubling both N and D instead would cost four times the rough budget.

questions.q: Explain to a teammate why a larger context can cause out-of-memory with identical model weights. Separate parameters, attention activations and KV cache.
rubric: Parameters are fixed learned tensors while actual request length varies within the configured capacity
Explicit dense score storage scales with B*H*T*T; FlashAttention changes materialization, not the definition of attention
A hypothetical full multi-head inference cache scales with 2*L*B*T*C times bytes per value, not T squared
Training also retains activations and optimizer arrays; the lab's generate function does not implement the estimated cache
A peak-memory measurement is needed for the actual serving or training implementation

questions.q: An internal document assistant misses evidence. A teammate proposes the biggest model available. Explain the diagnosis and apply it to a case where relevant documents are missing from the prompt.
rubric: Parameter count alone is not a quality guarantee; data, optimization, post-training and task evaluation matter
If source evidence is absent, first test retrieval and context assembly rather than assume weight scaling solves access
Use permission-appropriate source passages, citations and a held-out answer-quality evaluation
Compare model changes using fixed representative tasks, latency and memory constraints
Do not infer safety, authorization or factual correctness from fluent text or a lower language-model loss

recall.q: Why does this GPT block have a leading 12C^2 term?
recall.a: Attention projections contribute 4C^2, and the two fourfold-expansion MLP matrices contribute 8C^2. Biases and norms add 13C in this exact architecture.
One independent V by C output matrix. The same Parameter serves embedding lookup and vocabulary scoring; output computation still exists.

recall.q: Why is parameter count not peak memory?
recall.a: Dtype, gradients, optimizer state, activations, KV cache, buffers and runtime overhead also matter.

recall.q: What does 6ND estimate, and what is D?
recall.a: Rough dense-model training FLOPs. D is processed tokens, including repeats, not unique documents. Context attention and implementation details can make the estimate inaccurate.

recall.q: What did Chinchilla change in the scaling discussion?
recall.a: Under its studied training-compute objective, scaling data alongside parameters was better than growing parameters while holding training data nearly fixed. It is not a universal deployment optimum.
